transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m here because I keep losing my temper over little things. I’ve been snapping at people on operations calls, and even at my family at home. That’s not like me, and it’s starting to worry me.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or experiencing anxiety along with these temper outbursts?

Yeah… anxious, I guess. It’s like I’m on edge all the time. Any time I hear a forklift beep, or a compressor kick on, even the smoke alarm chirping at home, my whole body tightens up. I start looking around for exits and thinking about what could go wrong next.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I don’t know if I’d call it “down” exactly, but I’m not really enjoying anything. My wife will make dinner, the kids will be talking about soccer like everything’s normal, and I know I should feel happy to be there. But it’s like nothing in me responds. I’m just kind of sitting there.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things in your day-to-day life, like work, family, or responsibilities, even when there’s no clear problem?

I’m not sure it’s like regular worrying about bills or chores or that kind of thing. I haven’t really noticed it that way. It’s more just… I feel keyed up, but I can’t always point to one specific problem.
Do you find yourself feeling worried or anxious about a number of different things in your life, not just one specific problem?

I don’t think it’s a bunch of different things, no. I mean, I feel anxious a lot, but it doesn’t feel like I’m worrying about work and family and money all separately. It’s more just this general keyed-up feeling, if that makes sense.

So it’s more of a general anxious feeling rather than worrying about specific things—does this anxious feeling seem to come and go, or does it feel like it’s there most of the time, even when nothing stressful is happening?

It feels like it’s there most of the time, but it really spikes with certain sounds. Like if I hear a forklift beeping, or a compressor kick on, even the smoke alarm chirping at home, my whole body tightens up. I start looking around for exits or what could go wrong next. It’s hard to shut that off.
Is there ever a time when you feel completely at ease, or does the anxious feeling seem to be there even when nothing stressful is happening around you?

I don’t really feel completely at ease much lately. Even when nothing’s happening, it’s like I’m still waiting for something. And if I hear a forklift beep, or a compressor start up, or even the smoke alarm chirp at home, my body just locks up. I start scanning around, looking for exits, thinking about what could go wrong next.
Can you recall if this anxious feeling has been present most days for at least several months, even when things are going relatively well in your life?
No, not for several months. It’s been about three weeks now, since the valve failure and the injury at the facility. Before that I don’t remember feeling like this most days.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or ability to concentrate along with these anxious feelings and temper outbursts?

Yeah, sleep’s been bad. Most nights I’m just lying there with that alarm sound playing in my head. And when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up sweating from dreams about smoke and people yelling. By the morning it feels like I barely slept at all.
Can you tell me a little more about the valve failure and injury at the facility—were you directly involved, or did you witness it happen to someone else?

I’m not sure how much more I can say about that part. I don’t really have the details straight in my head. I know it was at the facility and it involved the valve failure and someone getting hurt, but whether you mean directly involved versus just seeing it happen… I’m having a hard time putting that clearly.
Can you clarify whether you were directly involved in the valve failure incident, or were you nearby when it happened to someone else?

I’m trying to answer that, but that’s the part that scares me. There are chunks I just can’t pull up—especially those seconds around the alarm and the shutdown. People keep telling me I did the right things, but I can’t clearly remember if I was right there in it or just nearby when it happened.
Since the incident at the facility, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought of it that way. I mean, I’ve been kind of keeping to myself, but I don’t know if I’m avoiding specific places or people because of it. Nothing clear comes to mind right now.
Since the incident at the facility, have you found yourself having sudden, vivid memories or flashbacks of what happened that feel like you're reliving it?

Yes. It just hits me out of nowhere. I can be sitting at the kitchen table or trying to answer emails at home, and suddenly I’m seeing that flash from the valve and the smoke in the aisle like I’m back there. It kind of pushes everything else out of my head for a minute.
Since the incident at the facility, have you noticed yourself feeling angry or having difficulty controlling your anger, especially when reminded of what happened?

Yes. That’s actually one of the reasons I’m here. I keep blowing up at people over things that shouldn’t be a big deal. I’ve snapped on operations calls, and I’ve snapped at my family too. That’s not how I usually handle things, and it’s been hard to control once it starts.
Since the incident, do you find yourself being more startled or reactive to sudden sounds or reminders of what happened, even if they’re not directly dangerous?

Yes. Sudden sounds set me off now. If I hear a forklift backing up, a compressor kick on, or even the smoke alarm chirp at home, my whole body just tightens. I start looking around for exits, checking what could go wrong next, even when I know I’m not actually in danger.
Since the incident, have you noticed that you’re more irritable or easily upset, even when you’re not reminded of what happened?

Yes. Even when nothing specific sets it off, I’m just on edge and I get upset way too fast. I’ll blow up over something small on an operations call, or snap at my family over nothing. That’s not how I used to handle things, and it bothers me.

Since the incident at the facility, have you noticed any lasting changes in your mood, such as feeling numb, being unable to experience joy, or having a hard time feeling safe or connected with others?

Yeah. I don’t feel much of anything good right now. My wife will make dinner, or my kids will be talking about soccer like everything’s normal, and I know I should feel happy to be there with them. But it’s like… there’s nothing in me that responds. I’m there, but I don’t really feel it.
Since the incident at the facility, have you noticed these symptoms getting worse when you're reminded of what happened, or do they also occur even when you're not thinking about the event at all?

It happens both ways, but the worst is when it just comes out of nowhere. I can be sitting at the kitchen table or trying to answer emails from home, not even thinking about it, and suddenly I’m right back there — seeing the flash from that valve and the smoke in the aisle. It just pushes everything else out of my head.
